newsitem.title: GERMANY: German police believe found millionaire's body.
newsitem.headline: German police believe found millionaire's body.

text.p: German police said on Saturday a body they had found in woodland outside Frankfurt earlier in the day was almost certainly that of kidnapped multimillionaire Jakub Fiszman.
"According to the information we have so far, we believe that in all probability, verging on certainty, the body is that of Jakub Fiszman," regional police chief Klaus Timm told a news conference.
Fizsman was kidnapped outside his office on October 1 and the last sign that he was alive came when he made a telephone call to a friend the following day.

Timm said the body was found partly covered by leaves and a fallen tree near in woodland around 50 km (30 miles) from Frankfurt. "I can't make on any statement on the cause of death or whether he was killed where he was found," he added.
He said a final identification had not yet taken place but the clothes on the body matched a description of what Fiszman was wearing when he was kidnapped.
Two suspects, 48-year-old Rainer Koerppen and his 26-year-old son Sven, have been in custody since Wednesday.
Timm said police were able to narrow down the search area after Sven Koerppen gave them more information on Friday night.
Fiszman's brother Georg paid a ransom of four million marks ($2.6 million) on October 10, but his kidnappers reneged on an agreement and failed to free him the following day.
Police recovered most of the ransom on Wednesday in the garden of an apartment in Wiesbaden owned by Rainer Koerppen's parents.
Tornado reconnaisance jets joined the search for Fiszman on Friday, using heat-seeking equipment and advanced cameras to scan the area for any sign of the missing man.
Police had said on Friday they were becoming more pessimistic about the fate of the 40-year-old businessman, whose family's fortune has been put at more than 400 million marks ($260 million).
